svg.text: A fenced write is one transaction: check the token, then write
Step 1 locks the session's bucket lease row and checks the token; if it isn't yours, the whole transaction rolls back.
One transaction (atomic)
Step 1 · checked UPDATE of the bucket row (token must match)
UPDATE bcs_task_leases SET fence_seq = fence_seq + 1
WHERE bucket = :b AND fencing_token = :mine -- 1 row
~25 sessions per bucket: the row is busy ~5 % of the time
Step 2…n · the durable writes for this session
run status · checkpoints · Task record · last_event_seq · unpublished · write_seq + 1
dispatch / delivery records (item 3) · durable timers
all in the same database as the lease row
Token matches
step 1 changes 1 row → steps run → COMMIT
the lock is held until COMMIT, so a claim
or transfer of the bucket cannot commit in between
S's write_seq tells a handoff successor what changed
Token is stale (someone claimed bucket b)
step 1 changes 0 rows → it all rolls back
caller gets LeaseLost →
stop driving b's sessions, evict them, never retry
Why a concurrent claim can't slip in between check and commit
A claim (or a handoff transfer) updates the same bucket row, so it waits until the in-flight fenced transaction commits,
then bumps the token. Every later fenced write by the old owner fails step 1. Must change exactly 1 row (ExecuteChecked).
Rules: same transaction · same database · one session behind its bucket's check · LeaseLost means stop · unknown commit outcome → read back, never blind-retry.
